**Published online:**
September 9, 2026 (Reuters)

**Geographic focus:**
United States (primary); with secondary references to Japan, Germany, United Kingdom

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [YES] — references 2022 Fed tightening cycle and YTD flow data through August/September 8
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — rising oil prices, inflation concerns, yield trajectory positioning
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — structural duration barbell strategy, government borrowing/spending concerns

**Synopsis:**
US bond ETF investors are rotating toward short- and intermediate-maturity debt, away from long-duration bonds, amid a global bond selloff. Rising oil prices are reigniting inflation fears while heavy government borrowing is pushing long-term yields to multi-year highs across major markets. Flow data confirms the trend: short-term bond ETFs are absorbing the bulk of inflows while long-term ETFs remain largely unloved. The rationale is that the yield curve inadequately compensates for duration risk, making intermediate bonds the sweet spot — offering upside if growth slows while limiting downside if rates rise further. JPMorgan AM describes this as a "duration barbell" strategy.

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?**
Sentiment: +55 (Hawkish lean — US Treasury yields near three-year highs, oil-driven inflation revival, long-duration bonds unloved, and the market is actively hedging against further rate increases rather than pricing in relief; the "duration barbell" reflects uncertainty but the dominant force described is upward yield pressure)
